summary.short: Regulates Law 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital) on children's protection in digital environments: age assurance, prohibited-content access, advertising, reporting and transparency duties for information technology providers, app stores and operating systems; institutes a national children's digital policy. In force on publication, 18 March 2026.
summary.long: Implements Law 15.211/2025 (ECA Digital) and institutes a National Policy for Promotion and Protection of Children's and Adolescents' Rights in the Digital Environment, with an intersectoral committee and a Federal Police notification triage centre (Arts. 1-8). Providers of information technology products or services directed at or likely accessed by children must prevent excessive use and manipulative design (Arts. 9-10). Providers of generative and conversational AI services must disclose synthetic interaction, prevent behavioural manipulation, assess algorithmic risk and apply safeguards (Art. 11). Prohibited content (e.g., alcohol, tobacco, gambling, pornography, loot boxes) must be kept from children through age verification (Arts. 14-19). App stores and operating systems must supply age signals and seek parental authorisation for app downloads (Art. 25). Age-assurance methods must meet data-minimisation and privacy rules, with ANPD regulating and certifying them (Arts. 24-30). Child-directed advertising, profiling and monetised child content are restricted (Arts. 31-35). Providers must report serious child-abuse content to the triage centre, remove it, and offer notification mechanisms (Arts. 36-43); ANPD accredits child-rights NGOs (Art. 44). Larger providers report notification data (Art. 45) and conduct child-safety impact assessments (Art. 47). Until ANPD regulates, manufacturers and importers of devices marketed exclusively to children must add a parental-supervision warning on packaging (Art. 50).

notes: The document is the Portuguese text as provided; its footer states it does not replace the text published in the DOU of 18.3.2026 (edição extra), which was not checked. Lei 15.211/2025 is not in the document, so its article references are recorded as cited, not verified. The text treats loot boxes both as prohibited content for children (Art. 15 § 1 VII) and as a feature to be age-gated (Art. 23); the text does not state how these provisions interact. Art. 45 sets a reporting duty for providers with more than one million registered users in the children's age range; this threshold is not coded here.
